images.caption: Figure 1:Motivation and central idea of SEEK.Top: GPT-6 Astra[29]acting directly keeps what the robot learns only in its working context and loses it once the task ends, so the next attempt may repeat the same mistakes; on a real robot, the last cube of a square is again grasped and set down, leaving a gap. Bottom: SEEK retains this execution knowledge across attempts as action-effect evidence (PAEB), including that of failed attempts, and reusable procedures (SEPP), while the model remains fixed; its next attempt pushes the cube in. Right: with GPT-6.2 Astra on 34 RoboDojo tasks, task score by category and model requests per episode of SEEK after 5 attempts and of the model acting directly[38].

Figure 2:Execution and self-evolution in SEEK.SEPP grounds reusable procedures in the current observationxtx_{t}and controls execution, while PAEB accumulates the resulting evidence. At steptt,ctc_{t}denotes the execution context used by the active procedure. In the progress panel, a check marks a goalgtg_{t}that the procedure verifies by itself before advancing, and the model icons mark the only steps where the fixed model is called: when a procedure requests help or execution stalls (red cross). When called, the fixed model retrieves evidence from PAEB to guide execution, by interpreting observations or proposing action candidates, or to revise the main program or operations. Across attempts, post-attempt review consolidates the policy, while scene-dependent state is initialized anew.

Figure 4:Case study on Deposit Coin.(a) After attempt 1, consolidation creates the rim-pinch operation (\scriptsize1⃝) from PAEB evidence. (b) Grasp verification (\scriptsize2⃝) is revised online in attempt 3 and retained. (c) Attempt 5 reuses both, with a test lift detecting an empty grasp (\scriptsize2⃝) and triggering a rim re-grasp (\scriptsize1⃝). Numbered frames mark the supporting procedure. Orange and purple arrows carry evidence and procedures to later attempts. In each SEPP card, the open tab is the changed operation, with additions in gold and removals dashed.
Figure 5:Real-robot setup and tasks.The Franka arm with its wrist and front cameras, and each of the four tasks in an example layout.
